subject: Texas AI Docket, Carousel No. 18, September 9th, 2026, Case managers beat Houston Methodist's discharge AI on the last day
body:
Case managers beat Houston Methodist's discharge AI on the last day

Carousel No. 18, September 9th, 2026

Did NOT meet the bar: 6.714 against 6.8. Read before posting.

This run did not merge, so the images below come from the run branch claude/daily-2026-09-09 rather than from main. They stop resolving if that branch is deleted.

What degraded

  • THE RUN HELD. It did not merge, and the record and the deck are on the branch rather than on main
    ask_pack's self-test measures the index every question pays for at 40,644 chars against a 40,000 ceiling. CI is red on it and CLAUDE.md says never merge until CI reports green on the head. Remove this run's three admissions and the index is 40,092, still over by 92, so the breach predates this run: main is 81 commits behind and the 2026-09-05 and 2026-09-07 runs never merged, so their admissions are counted here for the first time. scripts/site/ask_*.py is HUMAN lane, so both fixes the file itself prescribes, rolling a family up and moving the number, are out of this run's reach, and the file says raising the ceiling is never a fix anyway. The only daily-lane lever is cutting the record's own copy, which recovers under half of what is needed and would make ten items read unlike the other 105. Written up in knowledge/carousel/UPGRADE_BACKLOG.md.
  • THE DECK SHIPPED UNDER THE BAR at 6.714 against 6.8
    Five scoring rounds, which is the cap. Past the cap a run ships whatever the median is and says so. Judge spread 0.12, the tightest of the run. The weak criterion is variety at 5.5.
  • The light register breaches deck 14's avoid_next, which addressed this deck by name
    Deck median L* 71.1 with deck 14 at 73.1 still in the eight run window. check_register does not fail, because deck 14's named waiver subtracts it, which that waiver's own note says it must never do. Recorded as a breach, no waiver claimed, next deck required dark.
  • c10's three encounter counts were cut from the deck before anything was planned
    They print with a thin space inside the thousands and numeral_lint reads 21 710 as two numerals. The caption's close was rewritten in round 4 because it had been asking a question c10 answers.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Case managers beat Houston Methodist's discharge AI on the last day, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

A commercial clinician-assisted tool estimated when patients would go home. Houston Methodist's case managers beat it, and by more the nearer discharge got.

The authors say that is when an accurate date counts for most in bed management.

At admission the two were level on error, though the case managers matched the exact date more often. At 24 hours the case managers put 79.5% of estimates within one day of the true date. The tool put 37.9%. Between the two readings the case managers got better. The tool got worse, from 1.59 days to 1.93.

The authors then argue against themselves. Case manager estimates were part of usual care and visible to care teams, so they may be partly self fulfilling. The AI estimates were not enabled automatically.

No baseline patient demographic data were available. Which patients did it read worst?

#HoustonMethodist #JAMANetworkOpen #SQUIRE

2. The first comment

Sources. Every fact on every frame traces to one of these, all from the same record.

c1 Inpatient encounters at Houston Methodist Hospital discharged between August 1st, 2023 and February 28th, 2024. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13543018/
c2 At 24 hours, 79.5% of case manager estimations fell within 1 day vs 37.9% for AI estimations.
c3 Mean absolute error at 48 hours and at 24 hours, case managers against AI, with confidence intervals.
c4 At admission accuracy was similar between methods, and case managers matched the exact date more often.
c5 The dates came from a commercial clinician-assisted tool integrated with the EHR.
c6 AI-estimated discharge was comparable to usual care at admission but outperformed by case managers as discharge approached, when accurate estimations are most actionable for bed management.
c7 The strong admission correlation did not persist nearer discharge and should not be interpreted as evidence that the tool captured the same information clinicians use throughout the stay.
c8 Case manager estimates were part of usual care and visible to care teams, so they may be partly self-fulfilling. AI estimations were accessible in the EHR but not enabled automatically.
c9 Whether the AI's incremental accuracy in selected subgroups justifies the complexity of implementation warrants prospective, outcome-based evaluation.
c11 No baseline patient demographic data were available.
c12 The study followed the SQUIRE reporting guideline.
c13 Havish S Kantheti, MD, Connor Dolan, BS, Jordan Dale, MD.
c14 Published September 3rd, 2026, doi 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.32033.

The full study is at https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13543018/
The record entry is at https://texasaidocket.com/item/tx-2026-0129/

The machine changed itself

  • caption_check's first-person rule no longer reads a top level domain as a pronoun
    The City of Lubbock publishes at mylubbock.us, so this run's source page built to sources/mylubbock-us/ and the gate reported first person on nine strings that contain none: the hostname, the slug, the canonical URL, the title and four metadata fields. A period and a hyphen are both word boundaries. The exemption is anchored on the character in front, exactly like the two already in that pattern, and four self-tests prove both directions. Upgrade lane.
  • the caption ledger's three exclusion lists are derived rather than hand-appended
    opening_moves_recent, structures_recent and closing_moves_recent were stale in BOTH directions before this run touched them, which is the caption critic's standing finding. They are recomposed from the entries now, and this run's own moves were checked against them before being filed.
  • PROPOSAL, not built: inject computed.json into each frame at render time
    Two frames retyped compute.py's geometry this run and four scoring panels missed it. slide-05 drew 180 px per day against compute.py's 300 and slide-04 held run_depth 138 against 96, both under comments claiming they came from compute.py. render.py is under .claude/, which the host stops any unattended session from writing, so this is one a maintainer has to make.
  • PROPOSAL, not built: a gate that reads the SUBJECT of a sentence
    All three of this run's hard fails were an actor or a predicate the record does not license, and no gate in the suite reads a grammatical subject. It should extract the subject and main verb of every declarative sentence a frame prints and require that subject to be an agent of that act inside a cited claim's quote. It needs a parser and the eighteen shipped decks to tune against.
  • PROPOSAL, not built: caption_check should read brand.yaml's banned_phrases
    brand.yaml lists 76 banned phrases and caption_check does not read that key at all. The word 'actionable' shipped to two published surfaces of this deck with every gate green, and a judge found it. Anything inside a verbatim quotation has to stay exempt, because the house rule says a quote is never touched.

Each reverts on its own commit.

Notes

The record carries 115 items and every one was re-verified this run, 95 due and none rotten. Three were admitted: the Houston Methodist discharge study (tx-2026-0129), the Lubbock City Council's charter petition hearing of September 8th on an 18 month data center moratorium (tx-2026-0130), and ERCOT's market notice setting an October 6th workshop on large load curtailment under Senate Bill 6 (tx-2026-0131). The geography backlog is emptied and the stale exemption behind it is gone from docket_build. /questions/ was telling readers that three shut comment windows were open. schema.py kept its own copy of the window logic instead of importing the canonical window_state, so a page built from the same ledger disagreed with the item pages beside it. Fixed at source with self-tests in both directions. Five source behaviours were appended to the field log, including that capitol.texas.gov serves a rolling window rather than an archive, and that Legistar returns \r\n escaped inside its JSON.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck did NOT merge, so nothing here is on main and there is nothing to post. The links resolve against the run branch for as long as it exists.
